Chapter 7: System Testing

7.1 Testing Strategy, Methodology & Test Environment

Quality assurance for AssetDesk was executed through a comprehensive, multi-tiered testing strategy structured around the automated test pyramid. Verification combined white-box unit testing for business rules and state machines, black-box HTTP integration testing for REST API controllers, end-to-end browser automation for full user journeys, and defensive security assertion testing. Testing tools comprised Jest 29.7.0, Supertest 7.0.0, mongodb-memory-server 10.1.3, and Microsoft Playwright 1.50.0.

Table 7.1: Automated Test Environment Specifications
Environment Dimension Specification / Version Role in Verification Lifecycle
Operating System Darwin 24.6.0 (x64) POSIX-compliant continuous testing baseline environment
JavaScript Runtime Node.js v24.13.0 / npm 11.6.2 Execution engine for backend unit and integration test runners
Database Layer MongoDB Community Server v8.2.4 Isolated in-memory database instance (mongodb-memory-server)
Browser Engine Chromium 131.0 (Headless) Headless browser running 16 Playwright E2E tests at 1366×768
Test Runners Jest 29.7.0 & Playwright 1.50.0 Parallel test runners with Istanbul code coverage instrumentation
Quality Assurance Acceptance Criteria

The test strategy enforced four mandatory pass criteria prior to build approval: (1) 100% pass rate across all 272 automated test assertions with zero skipped or flaky tests; (2) Line and statement code coverage exceeding the 85% project contract threshold; (3) Complete traceability connecting all 20 Functional Requirements (FR-01..FR-20) to automated tests; (4) Average API query response latencies remaining strictly under 10ms for inventory pagination and summary endpoints.

7.4 Security Assertion Testing & Latency Benchmarks

Automated security assertion testing evaluated defenses against malicious injection, privilege escalation, and token tampering attacks. Table 7.6 details all 12 security test cases (100% passed). Table 7.7 reports operational REST endpoint latencies measured across 50 continuous test cycles.

Test ID Security Control Tested Attack Vector / Negative Test Case Defensive Guard Applied Result
SEC-01NoSQL Injection DefenseInjected {"$gt": ""} operator into login bodyExpress sanitizer strips $ operator → 400PASS
SEC-02JWT Signature TamperingModified JWT payload role claim to ADMINHMAC-SHA256 signature mismatch → 401PASS
SEC-03Token Expiration TrapDispatched request with expired JWT timestampTokenExpiredError caught by middleware → 401PASS
SEC-04RBAC Vertical EscalationEmployee token used to call POST /usersRole verification middleware rejects → 403PASS
SEC-05Horizontal Data IsolationEmployee querying another user's private ticketOwnership query filter returns 404 Not FoundPASS
SEC-06Credential Leak GuardInspected JSON payloads across all user endpointsMongoose toJSON transform deletes passwordHashPASS
SEC-07Brute-Force Rate LimitingDispatched 15 consecutive login requests from 1 IPSliding window limiter blocks 11th attempt → 429PASS
SEC-08Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)Submitted <script>alert(1)</script> in ticket titleStored as literal data; React escapes JSX renderPASS
SEC-09DoS Payload ProtectionTransmitted oversized JSON payload (> 100 KB)Body parser limits max payload size → 413PASS
SEC-10HTTP Security HeadersInspected response headers on API endpointsHelmet injects CSP, HSTS, X-Content-TypePASS
